newsitem.title: USA: U S West adds 742,000 access lines in 1996.
newsitem.headline: U S West adds 742,000 access lines in 1996.

text.p: U S West Communications Group said on Wednesday it added 742,000 access lines in 1996, 26 percent more than it added in 1995.
The company said it now has more than 15.4 million access lines in service, a 5.0 percent increase from last year, adjusted for the sale of certain rural exchanges.
This annual growth rate includes a 7.6 percent increase for business lines, a 4.0 percent increase for residential lines, and a 30.8 percent gain for residential additional lines.

The access line growth, coupled with staff reductions at the telephone company of more than 2,500 for the year, helped the company achieve a nine percent improvement in productivity, as measured by employees-per-10,000-access-lines.
Richard McCormick, chairman and chief executive of U S WEST Inc, said the company had a strong 1996 performance, especially in the fourth quarter.

"Top-line results are starting to pay off on the bottom line. That tells me we turned the corner in many respects in 1996 and can now enter 1997 with momentum and a real sense of optimism," McCormick said.
U S West posted fourth quarter net income of $0.65 per share on operating revenues of $2.60 billion compared to $0.59 per share on operating revenues of $2.44 billion.
The First Call quarterly estimate was $0.60 per share.
